31f10be8-568a-44f4-a5fd-64763717e190.title: thermite-lower: lower_spec_arg drops the byte-view for a FIELD-ACCESS bytes_eq String operand (&result.text / &b.text -> &TString, E0308) — blocks #276 Arc-2
31f10be8-568a-44f4-a5fd-64763717e190.description:
thermite-lower::lower_spec_arg lowers a `bytes_eq` String OPERAND that is a FIELD ACCESS (`&result.text`, `&b.text`) to a `&TString` reference instead of the `Seq<u8>` byte view (`result.text.data@`), causing E0308 at real verus. This blocks #276 Arc-2 (the editor's bytes_eq content pins, whose operands MUST name `result.text` / `b.text` — the Buffer's text field).

ROOT CAUSE (thermite-lower/src/lower.rs, `lower_spec_arg`, ~lines 7595-7646):
- The single-segment-path byteview rule (`if string_as_byteview && segs.len() == 1 && ctx.is_string(name)` -> `{name}.data@`) and the `&<single-segment-path>` ref-strip rule (`Expr::Ref { expr: Expr::Path(segs) } with segs.len()==1`) handle bare String idents (`&ins`, `&result`, `&a`) correctly.
- A String operand that is `Expr::Field` (`result.text`, `b.text`) or `Expr::Ref { expr: Expr::Field {..} }` (`&result.text`, `&b.text`) is NOT matched, so it falls to `lower_expr` and emits `&result.text` (a `&TString`) — wrong type for `bytes_eq(a: Seq<u8>, b: Seq<u8>, ..)`.

MINIMAL REPRO (verus-confirmed E0308 'expected Seq<u8>, found &TString'):
  struct Buf { text: String, cursor: u64 } inv cursor <= text.len() && text.len() <= 1_000_000
  fn ins(b: Buf, s: String) -> Buf
    req b.text.len() + s.len() <= 1_000_000
    ens result.text.len() == b.text.len() + s.len()
    ens bytes_eq(&result.text, &b.text, 0, 0, b.cursor)
    fx alloc
  { let head: String = b.text.slice(0, b.cursor); let tail: String = b.text.slice(b.cursor, b.text.len());
    Buf { text: head.concat(s).concat(tail), cursor: b.cursor + s.len() } }
emits `__thermite_bytes_eq(&result.text, &b.text, 0 as int, ...)` -> E0308.

The C8 demo (conformance/bytes_eq_demo.th) never tripped this — it uses ONLY flat String params / the whole result (all single-segment paths). The gap is field-access String operands.

FIX (in thermite-lower/src/lower.rs::lower_spec_arg only): when `string_as_byteview` and the operand is an `Expr::Field` (or `Expr::Ref` wrapping an `Expr::Field`) whose field type is `String`, emit `<base>.<field>.data@` (the `Seq<u8>` view), mirroring the existing single-segment `{name}.data@` rule. The field's String-ness check must use the in-scope struct/field type info (the same machinery the struct-invariant weave uses for `b.text`).

ACCEPTANCE: the minimal repro above certifies L3 through real verus; #276's editor.th `insert_str`/`backspace`/`render_frame` content pins certify L3; conformance/bytes_eq_demo.th + sum.th + bytes_eq_demo.cert.json byte-stable (no regression — only field-access operands change). Then #276 Arc-2 re-dispatches.

Surfaced by #276 Arc-2 (3rd STOP). #277 + #278 already landed and work; this is a distinct, narrow lowering gap.

17ad9261-524a-46f6-ab85-c8d6eb760869.author: Yffe
17ad9261-524a-46f6-ab85-c8d6eb760869.content:
Failing test at thermite-lower/tests/divergence_effects.rs::divergence_while_condition_callee_is_checked demonstrates the divergence.

Root: effects.rs check_block's `Stmt::Loop(l)` arm walks ONLY `&l.body` and never inspects `l.kind`. `LoopKind::While(Box<Expr>)` carries the loop condition expression, which can contain an `Expr::Call` to an effectful fn. lower.rs DOES lower the while condition (LoopKind::While(c) arm), so the call site is reachable codegen.

Authority: thermite-design.md §4.1 'a caller's row must subsume EVERY callee's row, checked at compile time'. A `fx pure` caller running `while effectful() {}` (effectful fx {alloc}) is currently ACCEPTED (false accept) instead of rejected with missing:[Alloc].

Fix is the generator's: extend the Stmt::Loop arm to also check_expr the While condition. Critic does not fix.

4414033d-8875-4767-a5e8-55945308e25d.content: Pin (the domain bridge, §4 theorem sketch). The sketch ends 'denote fuel ens (Env.bindInt { v with specs := R_item } "result" body)' and the doc asserts concreteness: 'the result-binding uses the SHIPPED Env.bindInt'. Against the spine: (a) TYPING — Env.bindInt : Env → String → Int → Env (Denote.lean) takes an Int; 'body' is an item body, i.e. a Block denoting via Thermite.Exec.bodyDenote : Block → State → Option ExecVal (Exec/Stmt.lean) in the BOUNDED domain. As written the sketch does not typecheck; the S_E→S_C value bridge (BVal.value : Int extraction) is stated nowhere. Bool-typed results have NO binding site (Env has ints/seqs/optres only; no bool sort, no bindBool); Option/Result-typed results (the #180 match-in-ens fragment, IN per §8) need an optres binding — no Env.bindOptRes exists in Denote.lean. (b) OPTION POSITION — bodyDenote = none exactly when an exec obligation fails (overflow/div-zero/oob). The doc takes NO position between (i) conjoining 'bodyDenote v = some r ∧ ens(r)' (then REQ-1's separate OVERFLOW class is redundant for Lean-discharged items — unreconciled) and (ii) hypothesizing 'bodyDenote v = some r → ens(r)' (then an always-overflowing body satisfies ens vacuously — sound ONLY IF the aux classes are mandatory-and-conjoined per item at the certificate level; NO such per-item conjunction rule exists anywhere in the doc: REQ-1 lists classes, REQ-2 fragments per class, REQ-3/REQ-4 are per-obligation; nothing forbids an engine certifying an item on the CONTRACT class alone). (c) ENV/STATE — the contract Env ({ints,seqs,optres,specs}) and the exec State ({env : ExecEnv{vars : String → ExecVal, slices : String → List BVal}, scope}) are disjoint structures; the v-to-State correspondence (params → in-range BVal cells at their widths, seqs List Int → List BVal) is specified nowhere. The spine's own theorems relate refDenote/denote and bodyRefState/bodyDenote SEPARATELY — this sketch is the FIRST artifact tying S_C and S_E/S_B in one statement, and the doc neither owns that novelty nor scopes the sketch to increment (ii)'s PURE-CONTRACT class (where 'body' could be denoted in S_C via intVal — a choice also unstated). Fix is generator's: state the bridge + the Option position + the conjunction rule, or scope the sketch to pure-contract and mark the bridge an open design obligation for increment (iv).

FIXED (#127): byte-view dispatch + generated-def emission are now SHAPE-keyed, not callee-NAME-keyed.

Root cause had TWO faces of the same name-keying bug:
1. callee_takes_string_byteview (lower.rs) keyed the String->.data@ rewrite on a fixed name set; a user spec fn named like a generated one got its &String self-call arg misrouted to .data@ (E0308).
2. program_uses_parse/_numfmt/_string_search keyed the GENERATED-def emission on a name match; a user 'spec fn is_digit(s: &String, ..)' spuriously materialized the generated is_digit(b: u8) ALONGSIDE the user's -> E0428 (name defined twice).

- user_string_spec_fn_names(program): program-wide SHAPE-derived set of USER spec fns declaring a String/&String param (the user namespace; shadows any generated name).
- callee_takes_string_byteview now excludes a callee in that set BEFORE the generated-name match (Ctx.is_user_string_spec_fn) -> a user String spec fn passes the &TString reference, never .data@.
- the three emission gates exclude shadowed names so a user-named collision does not emit the generated def.

Param-type signal: a user spec fn declares &String/String (is_string_ty sees through one borrow); the generated fns take Seq<u8> and are synthesized (not in program.items), so they still byteview.

77c31e45-4530-4038-aa61-8db6fc0b0772.title: Divergence: RATIONALE cage entry misstates seccomp-BPF mechanics (claims BPF cannot read argument registers; contradicts own Direction)

9ccf9585-7cbb-4168-9fd2-e6eda510e21d.author: Yffe
9ccf9585-7cbb-4168-9fd2-e6eda510e21d.content: RATIONALE 'cage' Limits: 'Classic seccomp-BPF compares seccomp_data.nr, not argument registers — so it cannot filter ioctl by its cmd... subject to TOCTOU on pointer arguments it does not inspect.' Factually wrong about the mechanism: struct seccomp_data exposes args[0..5] and classic BPF filters routinely compare argument VALUES (Chrome's sandbox filters ioctl by cmd this way). The true mechanism limit: BPF cannot DEREFERENCE pointer arguments (kernel forbids it precisely to avoid TOCTOU), so paths can't be scoped. As written it (a) attributes this filter's v0.1 implementation choice (nr-only) to seccomp-BPF itself, (b) muddles TOCTOU (BPF can't inspect pointed-to memory at all; TOCTOU is the documented reason dereference is prohibited), and (c) contradicts the entry's own Direction, which proposes 'a BPF_JEQ on the ioctl cmd register' — impossible if the mechanism 'compares only nr'. forge/src/sandbox.rs doc comment near TERM_SYSCALLS repeats the same error. An OS/systems reviewer catches this in one read.

7a22aadc-a9b0-40a3-b0f3-786fa8b86fff.title: thermite-lower: L1 exec-twin bytes_eq operand &-strip gap (build-side #279 mirror)
7a22aadc-a9b0-40a3-b0f3-786fa8b86fff.description:
SPILLOVER from #276 (Arc 2 editor content pins). #279 fixed the L3 SPEC byteview lowering of field-access bytes_eq operands. The L1 EXEC-TWIN call-site lowering has the analogous gap, UNFIXED.

ROOT CAUSE: thermite-lower/src/l1.rs::lower_expr_exec, Expr::Call string-arg arm. For a leading string arg it emits '{lowered}.clone()' where lowered=lower_expr_exec(arg). When the operand carries a leading & (&result.text / &ins / &b.text), lowered='&result.text' so '&result.text.clone()' parses as &(result.text.clone())=&TString, against the twin's owned param 'fn bytes_eq(a: TString, b: TString, ...)'. rustc E0308 at every &-prefixed conjunct. The C5/C7 comment's claim '(&TString).clone() yields owned TString' holds only when lowered is a bare ident.

REPRO: forge build a fn whose ens names bytes_eq(&result.text, &b.text, ...) over a Buf-wrapped String, --entry a no-param caller -> E0308 xN. The bare-field form 'result.text' builds clean (why #276 ships bare-field).

FIX: strip a single leading & from lowered before .clone() in the string-arg branch (exec-twin counterpart of #279's spec &-strip); cover &path/&field as #279 did spec-side.

IMPACT: low — both spec+exec accept the BARE forms, so #276 ships with the sanctioned bare-field spelling; the demo/REQ-18 &-prefixed spelling is currently check-only. Closing this makes the operand class build-symmetric.

81a5e2ad-f853-40da-a7c7-eefd34eb873e.title: Divergence: parser no-struct-literal context leaks into match arm bodies — a value-position struct literal in a clause-position match fails to parse (01-adts.md REQ-2/REQ-4)

3bd2950d-e762-4789-a08f-dda1e21410af.author: Yffe
3bd2950d-e762-4789-a08f-dda1e21410af.content:
Failing test at thermite-syntax/tests/divergence_adt_parse.rs::divergence_clause_match_arm_body_struct_lit_parses demonstrates the divergence.

ROOT CAUSE: in parser.rs, parse_clause runs the clause expression under with_no_struct_literal (so a trailing 'Name { … }' is a block, not a struct lit — correct for the HEAD). When that clause expr is a bare 'match e { … }', parse_match parses the scrutinee under with_no_struct_literal then parses each arm body via parse_expr WITHOUT re-enabling struct literals. The clause's no_struct_literal flag is still active, so an arm body 'Point { x: 1 }' (VALUE position) is mis-parsed: 'expected }, found {'.

The other bracketed contexts (parse_call_args, parse_index_arg, the LParen primary) correctly re-enable via with_struct_literal; match arm bodies (and, by inspection, the if/else block tails reached through this path) do not. This is exactly the binary_search-shaped 'ens match result { … }' clause — the corpus passes only because its arm bodies happen not to construct structs.

AUTHORITY: .design/basis/01-adts.md REQ-2 (Expr::StructLit construction) + REQ-4 (match in expression position; arm bodies are value position). The fix (generator): wrap the match arm-body parse in with_struct_literal in parse_match.

Scrutinee parse (with_no_struct_literal) and the { block delimiter are unchanged; context restored on exit (no reverse leak). Pinned test divergence_clause_match_arm_body_struct_lit_parses PASSES. The clean types (Sql/Public/Authorized) are ordinary Stage-1 newtype structs with ACCESSIBLE fields, so an Expr::StructLit (Sql { stmt: input.raw }) outside the declared #[boundary] door mints a clean type directly from a marked value. v1's 'emergent type-level enforcement' relied on the type system, but the type system does NOT prevent constructing a clean struct from a tainted/secret/unauthorized field. Either (a) a sealed / door-only-constructible clean type — the validator rejects an Expr::StructLit of a clean type outside its declared #[boundary] door (the type is constructible only via its door's return), OR (b) the v1.1 dataflow-propagation engine (REQ-4) — a StructLit reading a Tainted/Secret field yields a marked result, rejected at the sink. Either makes the door the only launder point.

The doc's v1/v1.1 line is mis-drawn: the barrier is not v1.1 dataflow nicety, it is REQUIRED for the v1 centerpiece to hold. Amend the doc (acto-doc-author) to either pull the barrier into v1 scope or stop claiming v1 is un-typeable.

590fe66c-9f9c-42ea-a7cc-0296159d00e7.content: Pin (kernel-checked, lean/Thermite/PinIntBottom.lean). §4 claims: 'denote can only make the obligation EASIER (more vacuously true) by bottoming a specCall to True, never harder' and an under-computed fuel₀ 'only adds a TRIVIALLY-TRUE conjunct (the bottomed-out instance), which cannot WEAKEN the conjunction'. Both are FALSE against Denote.lean: only the Prop-position bottom is True; the Int-position bottom is 0 (intVal: 'fuel+1, Expr.specCall' resolves… '| none => 0', catch-all '| _, _, _ => 0'), and the CANONICAL ens shape puts the specCall in Int position ('result as nat == spec_sum(xs)' — the doc's own flagship, quoted in Exec.lean's header). Counterexample (kernel-checks against the shipped spine, axioms standard): registry f(x)=g(x), g(x)=x (real-bodied, complete — the hard gate passes); ens = 'result == f(x)'; env x=1, result=1 (the CORRECT item). denote 2 ens env HOLDS (real content result = x); denote 1 ens env is FALSE (the inner call bottoms, intVal returns 0, the conjunct is 'result = 0'); hence ¬(∀ fuel ≥ 1, req → ens) — the §4 obligation form with an under-computed fuel₀ is FALSE for a correct item, not 'trivially-true-conjunct' padded. Corollary (value-dependent recursion, which the doc concedes makes fuel₀ under-computation unavoidable): for 'result == spec_f(xs)' with unfolding depth |xs| and v ∀-quantified over unbounded seqs, EVERY finite fuel admits an env with |xs| > fuel whose conjunct is false — the exported obligation is FALSE for the canonical recursive item at ANY fuel₀, so the ∀-fuel form is broken for exactly the registry machinery's headline case (no better fuel₀ computation fixes it; the form needs an env-dependent adequacy bound, a stabilization premise, or a Prop-position-only scope). Also false in passing: claim (2) 'an everywhere-non-terminating spec-fn is True by S itself' — in Int position S assigns 0, and the obligation becomes the contentful 'result = 0'. Note: cycle-2's #210 observation ('the ∀-fuel form itself stays sound', 'fuel₀ under-computation verified NOT soundness-bearing') analyzed only the Prop bottom; this finding supersedes that sub-claim.

b8a87d79-b973-47a6-97fa-07ac80a2bd9b.title: Restrict SpecTherm closure bodies to a flat predicate fragment (no nested combinators)

1426b0cc-79e7-4ef1-8091-bb37bef7f8fe.author: Yffe
1426b0cc-79e7-4ef1-8091-bb37bef7f8fe.content:
External reviewer (human + agent) caught a real gap in the 'no general quantifiers / quantifier-locked SpecTherm' thesis (§4.2/§6). Verdict: partly true, worth fixing; the 'just renamed it' framing overstates it.

WHAT HOLDS: a combinator lowers to a BOUNDED quantifier with a FROZEN trigger on the predicate application (forall_in(s,p) == forall|i| 0<=i<s.len() ==> #[trigger] p(s[i])). Bounded range kills unbounded-quantifier blowup; frozen trigger removes Verus's heuristic trigger-inference variance (a primary SMT-discontinuity source). For a FLAT closure body this genuinely locks instantiation.

THE HOLE (reviewer is right): the closure body is currently UNrestricted and can contain ANOTHER combinator -> nested bounded quantifier -> the composition reintroduces multi-quantifier instantiation interaction. Our loop-3 thermite-spec validator currently ACCEPTS this (its critic tested forall_in(xs, |x| exists_in(ys, |y| y==x)) as valid). So the cage has exactly the described hole.

FIX (a strengthening, not a retreat): restrict SpecTherm closure bodies to a FLAT predicate fragment -- comparisons, arithmetic, boolean ops, field/index, and NAMED spec-fn calls -- but FORBID a nested combinator call inside a combinator's closure. Invariant becomes honest: 'every quantifier is a bounded combinator with a frozen trigger; composition happens only via named spec fns (dec-measured, auditable), never anonymous nested quantifiers.' Enforce as one new reject in the thermite-spec validator (which today over-permits) + clarify §4.2 + .design/spec/spectherm-combinators.md. Corpus is UNAFFECTED (sum/binary_search closures are flat: |x| x != needle etc.). Caveat: a flat closure may still call a named spec fn that internally quantifies -- depth is named+bounded, not zero; we kill anonymous arbitrary nesting, the unpredictable part.

Touches #2 (validator) + the design docs, NOT #5/forge. Could empirically demonstrate the flat-vs-nested distinction in real verus before implementing.

586d653f-a3bf-4d77-8a2d-cb96383eb6a2.content:
Failing tests at thermite-spec/tests/divergence_adt_validate.rs::divergence_lowercase_variant_bypasses_exhaustiveness and ::divergence_lowercase_arm_masks_unhandled_variant demonstrate the divergence.

ROOT CAUSE: parse_path_pattern (thermite-syntax/src/parser.rs) disambiguates a single-segment match-arm pattern into Pattern::Enum vs Pattern::Binding by FIRST-LETTER CASE alone ('an uppercase-initial single segment is a zero-field enum pattern', else a binding). But parse_enum places NO casing constraint on a variant DECLARATION (take_ident('a variant name')), so an enum may declare a lowercase variant. A lowercase variant named in a match arm parses as Pattern::Binding (a catch-all); variant_pattern_name returns None for it; check_match_exhaustiveness then infers no matched enum (or treats the arm as a wildcard), and a genuinely non-exhaustive match over a declared enum is ACCEPTED (Ok(())).

AUTHORITY: .design/basis/01-adts.md REQ-5 (NonExhaustiveMatch{missing}) + REQ-12 (handled-or-loud compile-time tooth — 'a non-exhaustive match does not compile'). R-DEFER-9.

CASE 1: enum E { foo, bar } ; match e { foo => 0 } -> expected NonExhaustiveMatch{missing:[bar]}, actual Ok(()).
CASE 2 (worst): enum Shape { Circle(u64), Rect{w,h}, tri } ; match s { Circle(r) => r, tri => 0 } -> Rect modeled-but-unhandled, expected NonExhaustiveMatch containing Rect, actual Ok(()).

The fix root cause lies in the parser/validator boundary (variant-name casing is not load-bearing in the design); the validator must not treat a lowercase ident matching a declared variant as a catch-all. This divergence requires the generator/fixer to resolve; the failing tests are the block.

ROOT CAUSE: `ens_implied_by_req` in forge/src/vacuity.rs returns `Some(idx)` on the FIRST ens clause that equals req or a req conjunct — i.e. it rejects when ANY clause is implied. The governing authority requires the WHOLE postcondition conjunction be implied.

AUTHORITY: .design/forge/vacuity-triage.md REQ-3 — '(c) reject ... defined as: EVERY ens clause's Clause.expr is structurally identical (PartialEq) to ... the whole req ... or one of the conjuncts of req'. thermite-design.md §7.1 — 'ens is syntactically implied by req alone -> reject' (the whole ens). OQ-4 confirms 'ens true + ens result == x ... carries a real conjunct'.

INPUT 1: req x > 0 && x < 10 / ens x > 0 / ens result == x  (fx pure, non-slag).
INPUT 2: req true / ens true / ens result == x.
EXPECTED: NOT an EnsImpliedByReq reject (result == x is a real obligation not implied by req; the whole ens is non-vacuous -> proceed to L3).
ACTUAL: cert.reject.cause == 'EnsImpliedByReq' (level L0) — the legitimately-stronger contract is wrongly rejected.

The fix narrows the (c) predicate to fire only when EVERY ens clause is req-implied. Control test ens_fully_implied_by_req_still_rejects_c (sole implied clause -> genuine (c) reject) guards against regressing the true-positive (oracle ens_conjunct_req). Tests must go green WITHOUT #[ignore] (R-DEFER-3).

Two readings, both defective. (A) As literally written, ∀ (env : Env) quantifies env.specs too — then the hypothesis only requires names resolve to SOME SpecFn, never pinning the REAL bodies, so the obligation quantifies over wrong-body registries (unprovable wrong statement) and is incoherent with EXP's 'the EXPORTED Env.specs registry'. (B) Intended reading (concrete exported registry, value-bindings quantified): the hypothesis is a closed decidable proposition about the emitted registry; an exporter that OMITS a called spec-fn makes it FALSE and the whole obligation is provable from the false premise — a registry-population bug self-certifies kernel-clean. The only guard the doc gives is EXP arm-by-arm INSPECTION ('paired with EXP registry faithfulness'), i.e. the trust item whose failure mode IS the omission. Sound alternatives the doc did not choose: (a) exporter-side hard gate — export FAILS mechanically when calledSpecFns(item) ⊄ dom(registry), so the theorem never carries the premise; (b) decide/rfl-discharged resolution lemmas emitted alongside (omission fails to compile). Secondary: the soundness paragraph's claim (1) 'every specCall … is fully unfolded at every fuel in range, so the => True arm is NEVER taken' is false for recursive spec-fns (static nesting depth ≠ value-dependent unfolding depth; Denote.lean: body 'MAY contain further specCalls'), though the ∀-fuel form itself stays sound. fuel₀ under-computation verified NOT soundness-bearing (the doc's parenthetical is correct).

dcaf84e1-8249-49c2-8ad3-5e3c30d463cc.content: Root cause: `as` binds tighter than the binary/unary operators in both Verus and Rust, but every cast-emit site in the lowering used a bare format!("{inner} as {ty}") / format!("{lowered} as usize"). Sites fixed in lower.rs + l1.rs: the Expr::Cast arm, the byte_at/slice 'as usize' coercion, the split 'as u8' coercion, and lower_index_arg's combinator 'as int'.
